# Home/runtime declaration fixture

This overlay reuses the invented five-seat Harbor/Orchard configuration, using its relative resource paths and the current shared Structure, Access, Agents and Host bodies. It adds Homes and Runtime, with no Identity grant. No real account, credential or agent home is referenced.

```sh
bash tests/fixtures/home-runtime-workplace/prepare.sh /absolute/new/config
```

The destination must be new and its parent must exist. The script copies source only: no PLAN, BUILD, runtime file, secret value or generated home. It does not call the reader/frame or start a server. The materialized workplace.json lists the six selected bodies. The default socket is not selected.

Navigator has a kept home, two extra variables (cache and the home itself via dot), and the root-relative seed path tools/seed-home. Gardener has a scratch home with a cache variable. The existing two none selections stay none. Four RUNTIME files each add one distinct environment name at workplace, office, room and seat scope. Watch's ordinary environment deliberately assigns dummy NAV_HOME/NAV_CACHE values; managed home variables must replace those when the frame starts the seat. No supplied runtime value is authored.

For a later isolated runtime rehearsal, first copy the existing reader-workplace/root support tree under the new root, then add this fixture's root/tools/seed-home. The seed merely writes its declared-directory arguments, in order, to its own provided home. It is a support executable outside the configuration input closure and must exist at the root-relative path; this source stop never invokes it through the frame. A private dummy-home safety probe checks its file replacement without building or starting a workplace. Ordinary tool directories and data must be supplied before build/up, not replaced by empty claims of functioning tools.

The first stop validates declaration formation and the emitted recorded terms. The independent expected events, per-seat decisions, malformed-source cases, frame refusals and later runtime cases are frozen privately before native measurement. Their outcomes are not disclosed in this repository during comparison. Runtime-file representation belongs to the frame contract; no guessed secret-bearing file format is published here.

No statement here claims that native parsing enforces frame conflicts, home isolation, seeding, runtime-value secrecy or persistence. See docs/homes-runtime.md for the boundary. Class restrictions are ordinary Typify declarations, not a specialized home or environment implementation in the reader.
